thread:
elaine: Quick Q — where do I look for slow TTFT traces / tokens/sec drops? Saw a spike in p95 on staging around 18:10 and need the usual hunting checklist.

matt: Start with the Grafana "Inference -> Latency by route" dashboard. Look at TTFT (time-to-first-token) panel and set the time window to 30m. The panel is at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inf-latency.

matt: For query: use Prometheus metric `redwood_inference_ttft_seconds` split by `model` and `route`. Example PromQL:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))
```
This gives p95 TTFT per model+route.

jasper: Also check `inference_tokens_per_second` for throughput drops — panel "Tokens/sec (ingress)". If tokens/sec drops while p95 spikes, likely underprovisioning or queueing.

kevin: For traces, use Tempo: https://tempo.redwood.internal/search. Filter by `route` tag and time. Look for long queue time vs compute time. If queue_time >> compute_time it's batching/scale issue.

anne: Logs: Kibana index `inference-*`. Search for `level:ERROR` and `route:<route>` around the spike. Also grep for `kv-cache:miss` — cold cache can inflate TTFT.

matt: If you want a quick TTFT vs tokens/sec correlation, run this PromQL in Explore:
```
# p95 TTFT for the route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) and on(route) avg(rate(inference_tokens_per_second[5m])) by (route)
```
(note: using `and` is just for eyeballing; better to graph them separately with shared Y axis.)

elaine: Nice — for alerting, what thresholds should I propose? p95 TTFT > 800ms? or model-dependent?

kevin: Model-dependent. Base guideline: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms for small models. For large-gen models p95 < 1500ms might be acceptable. Also create an alert for sustained tokens/sec drop: `tokens/sec < 50% baseline for 3m` to catch infra issues.

jasper: Add a secondary alert on trace sampling: if avg queue_time / avg compute_time > 3 for 5m, page oncall. (We have a template in the observability runbook.)

anne: Quick note — when you post the incident thread, include both a TTFT chart and a tokens/sec chart and one representative trace ID so SRE can triage.

elaine: Got it. One more: where's the canonical runbook for TTFT investigations?

matt: Runbook is in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/internal/observability/ttft-runbook. It has the checklist: dashboards, PromQL copy-paste, trace grep, Kibana queries, and playbooks for canary vs production.

sre-bot: ALERT (staging): high_ttft_p95 firing for route=/chat/stream (p95=1.2s) — alert id: S-4312 — see https://alerts.redwood.internal/S-4312

elaine: That alert is the one I saw. I'll follow the runbook and paste findings here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: If you want, I can add a temporary Grafana panel that overlays tokens/sec and p95 for that route so it's easier to spot correlation.

elaine: Please do — that would speed things up. I'll open a ticket and link it here when done.

matt: Also, if you suspect model variant fallback, check the model routing logs (`route_events` stream) for `fallback_to_variant` entries — can cause higher latency.

elaine: Perfect. Will update in ~30m with traces + charts.

anne: FYI, billing note: large p95 spikes on prod during peak could cost a lot due to extra tokens; if you see sustained issues, ping finance for possible throttling options.

elaine: Noted. Thanks everyone.
